images.title: Bisecting an angle
images.purpose: Show the construction that bisects an angle XOY, with the equal lengths marked.
images.composition: The vertex O at the lower left, the two arms opening to the right, the bisector between them.
exact_structure: A vertex O at the lower left with two dark rays: OY going to the right and slightly up, OX going up and to the right, about 60° apart.
A grey (#6B7280) arc centred at O cutting OY at A and OX at B; OA and OB each carry one tick mark.
A grey (#6B7280) arc centred at A and a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at B, of the same radius, crossing at C inside the angle; AC and BC drawn as thin dashed lines, each with two tick marks.
A teal (#0072B2) ray from O through C.
Two small reddish purple (#CC79A7) angle arcs at O, one between OA and OC and one between OC and OB, of equal size.
Labels O, X, Y, A, B and C.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: OA = OB and AC = BC, so SSS makes the two halves of the angle equal.
